The acoustic cloak is a concentric cylindrical shell composed of alternating layers of water and Methyl Nonafluorobutyl Ether (MNE).
MNE has a mass density of 1501 kg/m³ and sound velocity of 584 m/s; water has a mass density of 1482 kg/m³ and sound velocity of 998 m/s.
The cloak operates effectively in the kHz frequency range, with simulations performed at 29 kHz.
The cloak inner radius (R1) is 15 mm and outer radius (R2) is 35 mm.
Finite element method (FEM) simulations in 2D were used to analyze acoustic pressure distribution and scattering.
The composite lattice structure has constant water layer thickness but gradually decreasing MNE layer thickness.
Increasing the number of layers beyond 20 does not significantly improve cloaking performance.
The effective bulk modulus and density of the multilayer system are calculated using reciprocal bulk averages and weighted averages of individual layers.
The multilayer cloak reduces scattered acoustic pressure significantly compared to no cloak.
The composite lattice cloak outperforms a 20-layer multilayer cylindrical cloak in reducing acoustic scattering.
The cloak is designed using effective medium theory to treat the multilayer as an anisotropic medium.
The acoustic cloak can hide objects of any shape inside the cylindrical cloaking region.
The design avoids the need for exotic metamaterials with anisotropic mass density and bulk modulus that are difficult to fabricate.
The cloak works for both transverse and longitudinal shear waves without incident angle limitations.
The Helmholtz equation with anisotropic density tensor governs the acoustic wave propagation in the cloak.
The multilayer structure consists of alternating layers with thicknesses d1 and d2, typically equal in multilayer cloaks.
The composite lattice structure gradually varies layer thickness to optimize cloaking performance.
The cloak is scalable and can be designed for different wavelength ranges by adjusting layer thicknesses.
The study uses MNE due to its favorable properties: non-flammable, colorless, non-toxic, low vapor pressure, and transparent.
The cloak design can be fabricated more easily than metamaterial-based cloaks due to the use of natural isotropic materials.
